concept.title: What Is a Password Manager?
concept.shortdesc: A password manager generates, stores, and manages strong, unique passwords in an encrypted vault to improve your overall account security.

conbody.p: Strong passwords—those that are long, random, and unique—are essential to personal and university cybersecurity, but memorizing a distinct complex password for every online account is impractical. Storing passwords as plaintext in physical notes or unencrypted digital files also exposes your accounts if your device is lost or compromised.

section.title: How a Password Manager Works
section.p: A password manager protects and simplifies your login credentials in three primary ways:

ul.li: Generates strong passwords: Creates long, random passwords for each account so you do not have to memorize or reuse credentials.
Autofills login fields: Enters your saved usernames and passwords automatically on trusted websites and applications.
Encrypts your credential vault: Stores your passwords in an encrypted vault protected by a single master password and multi-factor authentication (MFA).

section.title: Choosing a Password Manager
section.p: When selecting a vetted password manager, verify compatibility across all of your devices and decide between two storage options:

ul.li: Cloud-based storage: Syncs your encrypted vault across devices over the internet.
Locally maintained database: Stays directly on your device and requires regular backups to separate storage media.

section.note: NC State staff and faculty must use only university-approved password management tools for storing institutional credentials, whereas students may select vetted personal password managers for their non-university accounts.
